steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Approaching Second Army territory.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Boss, should we keep our pace and press on?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Keep going.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: ...Hey, what if—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Don't worry. We're through the front lines, so it's smooth sailing from here. You've heard him many times, haven't you? Always stops whenever we might hit back.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Kuznetsov's got a strange mind, but he's smart. Might treat us like trash, but he'd still use us until we're all used up before throwing us away.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Also, he cares for his reputation. Refusing to change his station to 'protect the north', marching outside Grypherburg without orders to 'suppress the rebellion'...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Letting his own warships be destroyed on the front lines during an armistice because of 'recklessness'? Doesn't sound reasonable at all.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Your astute and logical analysis would make one think you're close to him, even though we've only been serving Kuznetsov for barely two years.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: How can I feed you lot if I can't even manage to ask around about our superior?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Back on topic. Since we're safe now, we no longer have to worry about the Second Army coming after us.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: But their vanguard battalion is right there.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Oh, right. Send our identification code to their command center at once.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Did you only just remember to do that?!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I tried earlier, but we were out of range.

steps.name: Voice from the Speakers
steps.text: —Bzzzzt—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Put it through to the speakers.

steps.name: Voice from the Speakers
steps.text: Re...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: The signal can't possibly be this bad, when we're already this close?
It is silent. Nothing comes through for several seconds—terrifying for those in the midst of war.
Everyone subconsciously straightens their backs as their breaths echo throughout the cabin.
If this is not a signal problem on the receiving end...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...Send it again.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: We already did.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Should we switch to the contingency plan?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: We're too close for that. It's too late to fight them now, we couldn't do much.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Safety first. Go—

steps.name: Voice from the Speakers
steps.text: Received.

steps.name: Voice from the Speakers
steps.text: Identity verified.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Received.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: We will be gone in two hours.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Chief.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Huh... wuh? That's new. You've never called me that ever—

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Come with me for a bit.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: 'Don't worry'? 'Smooth sailing'? Yebat ty, What's got you acting like a frightened little boy, then?

spans.text: , What's got you acting like a frightened little boy, then?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: It's different when I might drag everyone down with me.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Besides, that's was the past... I have no clue what deal he's done with the Second Army.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Perfect, because I rather not care about that now. What's important is whether you're going to tell the others or not.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...I didn't expect us to make it past the front lines, actually. I thought everyone would split and run off on their own, at which point it wouldn't matter.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Expectations and reality, completely different things. You'll have to tell them what you told me, unless you want them to die.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I don't want to send anyone to their deaths.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Yourself included?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Do I look like I have a death wish?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Who knows? I wasn't the one who personally escorted Lieutenant Sirka ten miles away, claiming I only went for a walk.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Alright, I won't die either. We good?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Let me think...

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Chief, I'm serious. None of us are cowards. I think they deserve the truth.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: If this is your own mission, or even if it's just to save one of our comrades... I think the risk of death will be the least of their concerns.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: In any case, you should let them know.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: They'll be able to intercept a broadcast from the ship, so let's get everyone on the mid-deck first.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I'll think about how I should break the news.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: This must be the first time we've done so many meetings in a single day, and everyone's here too, even those on the night shift—

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Shh. Just hear what the Boss has to say.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: It's definitely something important.
The crowd instantly goes quiet.
Scioppa stands on a makeshift platform, composed of empty vodka crates stacked on top of each other. He manifests his Arts, quickly creating a soundproof space covering the entire deck.
He turns around, the light of his enchantment subtly flickering under the sun as it transmits his voice clearly to the crowd.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Listen up.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: First, I must apologize to you all.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Soldier in the Back
steps.text: (Whisper) You hear that...? What for?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I'm sorry for not telling you the true reason for this expedition.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I won't explain how I came to that decision, but as your commander, I am responsible for my decisions, and since my reason for hiding the truth no longer exists—

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Boss, just tell us already. What is it?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: The truth is... this time, Sechin has not voluntarily accepted the order to seize the First Army's new weapon.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: This is also, essentially, a suicide mission.
He finishes with a deliberate pregnant pause to give the crowd time to process his words, expecting a wave of questions, but there is only silence.
Countless eyes look at him with the same expression. On the plains, on the battlefield, here and now, they have not changed.
Their trusting gazes seem to weigh down on him, and he suddenly realizes how tongue-tied he is now.
Making a speech, telling the truth—it now seems so arduous.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...So, that is why...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I swear to you...
As he struggles to find the right words to say, he notices Oleg has moved.
Oleg is now next to the platform, and he pats the young man on the back with his large hands that used to knead dough daily, almost knocking his leader off the platform.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Hey—

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Go on. Everyone's listening.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Say what you have to say, whatever it is.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I took on this mission because the Fourth Army has information on the whereabouts of some of our old comrades who left us upon becoming Infected.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Just before we shipped out, Lieutenant Sirka was seized by Kuznetsov's men.

steps.name: Soldier in the Back
steps.text: —Lieutenant Sirka?

steps.name: Soldier in the Back
steps.text: I think she was a quiet one... that Sirka?

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: We have to save her.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Yeah, boss. Why don't we go rescue her right now?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: That's the trouble. I don't even know where she is, I've only heard her voice over comms with Kuznetsov.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: So, our usual method of sneaking in, killing, rescuing, and getting out won't work here.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: So that only leaves me one path to take...

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: I'm not afraid to die. I'll ambush Evgeny and force Sirka's whereabouts from his dying breath! Maybe I can't do it alone, but I'm sure there are others willing to join me—

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: I know we can come up with a plan.

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: Count me in!

steps.name: Angry Soldier
steps.text: Me too!
The responses echo in the soundproof bubble. From the highest point on the deck, the man looks on as the cacophony of voices nearly take physical form, and shakes his head.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: It's impossible. I know you're all more than willing to kill for this, but no.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Why?!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: If I hadn't agreed to his demands, we'd never be able to save Sirka, and I couldn't protect the rest of you either.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: We can protect ourselves!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Could you protect yourselves from a whole unit of war casters?

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Before I decided to bring you all into the Fourth Army, I probed around and found out about a team, practically doing the same thing we do.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Kuznetsov's personal guard. A special task force composed of elite war casters.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: You mean... a whole unit as strong as you?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I'm nothing to them.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Leithanians use Infected as Arts units, but Ursus has researched the limits of using uninfected as casters, forcing them to use the tiny amounts of Originium within them as a catalyst.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: To reach their limit and to use the terrifying Arts units inside them, they endure the pain with drugs and body modifications, and this makes them adaptable to all sorts of combat scenarios.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: But this way, the Arts unit ends up consuming the user instead, turning their faces into a blur, their voices garbled.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: That's an easy way to contract Oripathy.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: War casters can never be Infected, to keep the Ursine army pure.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Whether it happens accidentally or taking a shortcut, you can bet those Infected get tossed down some random mine shaft.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Those who survive and join the army... even a dozen, or just a few of them, have enough firepower to replace a whole division.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: That's how strong they are.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Even if you wouldn't usually set up a unit of just war casters, seeing as it would limit their battlefield adaptability.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I thought we had it good then, figured they were a safety net for us. But when we went against the Fourth Army...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I finally understood how they came out of the Great Rebellion unscathed.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Fine! We can't beat them head-on or ambush them, so... what do we do? Sirka—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Don't worry, I won't leave her, or anyone else behind.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I just wanted to tell you all the truth, and then I have something to propose—or maybe I should say, a decision to announce.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I will cut all communication with the base, and falsify the Volnov's location while I stop the ship's operation, for an hour.

spans.text: I will cut all communication with the base, and falsify the
's location while I stop the ship's operation, for an hour.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: During this time, everyone is free to leave for nearby Volniki. Ultimately, this ship will function with a skeleton crew.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: We'll cut down on energy use as we continue to Zelgrad to secure the new weapon, which we'll use to negotiate with Kuznetsov and rescue Sirka.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Those willing to stay, throw your tags in the container.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: My brothers and sisters: when you chose to leave home, to join me with your passion and hope, I promised you this I wouldn't let anyone die in vain.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: We will not die like weeds, like fins, or fowlbeasts pulled, speared, or captured.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Because our lives have value. We are more than food for the monster we call war—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: We must be free, and not only living the freedom granted by the worthies above.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: We have another choice beyond fighting or dying.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Did you count all the votes?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Here, take a look.
He hands over an open barrel of vodka—completely empty.
Scioppa stares at the darkness within and sighs.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Didn't think I was so unpopular that nobody would want to stay.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Come on! I'm sure you know what it means—no one here wants to leave, not a single soul!

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Who would even think of leaving after listening to the sentimental garbage that just came out of your mouth?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Well, some of them will have to leave anyway. The ship doesn't have enough fuel to operate at full speed or reach the satellite city in time.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Why don't you just tell everyone your plan to abandon the Volnov and go back to Kuznetsov to settle the score?

spans.text: Why don't you just tell everyone your plan to abandon the
and go back to Kuznetsov to settle the score?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Because we should scatter our numbers to the Volniki, so Kuznetsov won't be able to catch all of us, if things go south.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: We can't put everyone in danger just to rescue Sirka, even if everyone's willing to throw their lives away.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Oh, so it's just gonna be me and you?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Come on now. You know most of them haven't spoken to Sirka even once. I can't expect the same of them as I do of us.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Enough. Hand out supplies according to the list, and have them leave once the ship stops.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: You stubborn—

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: —Chief, incoming urgent transmission from command!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: (Whisper) Closure isn't in here!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Amiya, don't lean backwards, or you might fall off the truck! Hang onto the frame and shift towards the front.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: It's pitch-black here without the streetlights. All we've got is our headlights, but at least we shook our pursuers.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But Closure—

options: Closure will be fine until the military catches us all.
We need to move fast and find the Sarcophagus.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Car's stopped.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Where... are we now? I think maybe we're underground—

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: We are.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: How are you feeling, Raidian?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I stopped my Arts when we got near that wall, so I am fine now.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Say, Amiya. I did not notice until now, but there is an issue with this vehicle.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: There is an electrical signal from someone besides ourselves and the driver. It is messy, but I'm sure—

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: (Whisper) Wait, we have to hide!

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: (Whisper) Keep close to me!

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: You're late.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: (Shieldguards... what are they doing down here?)

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Sir, there was an explosion on the other side of the wall, and I don't know what caused it, but please, if you could just say I was on time... I have one more delivery to make...
The man in worker's clothing keeps taking out thin and round objects from his pockets, trying to stuff them into hands of the heavily armored soldiers.
His efforts bear no fruit as the discs silently roll to the ground.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: You have broken the rules, so we no longer need you.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Take him away.

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: No—NO!

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: I won't be late next time, I promise—
The remaining Shieldguard stands there for a moment before dialing into his communicator.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Cancel the alert.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Have those below haul the goods away.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Six floors underground.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Hm, he left. If they've stationed heavy troops here, this probably means we're close to our target.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: If they're gonna get someone to haul the vehicle away, should we hide in the carriage?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: We do not know where it might go, so we'd best find the way ourselves.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Raidian, you said you noticed another electrical signal on the vehicle...?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: ...Hold on...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Not anymore.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What? Really?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I would not lie to you. This might mean that the one I detected before has met with misfortune.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Mon3tr, can you open the door?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: It's harder than—

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: ...I thought...
Neatly stacked fertilizer bags fail to conceal two human figures slumped on top of them.
One bears a frightening face, riddled with green scars and festering wounds, but the other has a peaceful expression, body covered in orange stones.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...! That patient—

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I'll go take a look.

options: Is this the patient you were talking about before?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I think so. But it seems like his Oripathy has worsened.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The density of the crystals on him too... it may be an acute infection, but to deteriorate this fast...?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Also, wasn't he—shouldn't he be at the clinic?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: He's dead, Amiya.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: For more than twelve hours at least, too.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: How? Wasn't there... a doctor?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: As for the other... his symptoms look similar to the one you mentioned earlier.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: There are marks on his neck, and the bag was ripped open. Seems like he strangled himself, which is why no one outside heard him.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: ...I'm guessing the Doctor is asking why they're in a 'fertilizer truck'.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Because this place doesn't actually store fertilizer.
Mon3tr moves, and several bags burst open.
No fluids or particulates spill from the bag, only frozen and mutilated... limbs.
Dark yellow crystals encrust the surfaces—Perhaps they were stuffed into these waterproof fertilizer bags according to certain criteria.
No one wants to even consider what they might be.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: How—
Raidian steps in, blocking Amiya from looking on any further.
Mon3tr finishes checking the truck carriage interior, and stands up, closing her eyes briefly.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: ...Infected. All of them.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Blood Originium-Crystal Density levels still climbing. This truck is practically a huge ticking time bomb—

options: Come back here. Thanks for checking.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Amiya, the one with green bruise marks shares symptoms with those infected by airborne Originium dust caused by bio-energy disequilibrium after a Sarcophagus overload.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: However, you need loads of energy and extremely destructive usage to overload a Sarcophagus, so an accident like this is extremely unlikely.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: This may well mean that the Sarcophagus's basic functions have gone completely out of control.

options: That means... it's lost its restorative capabilities?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Doctor, I refuse to prepare for the worst.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: But my observations so far have indicated the bio-dust is still leaking from the Sarcophagus, with unthinkable consequences if we don't stop it soon.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: It could come to a point where we'll have to destroy the Sarcophagus to stop it from spreading further.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: ...Although that would mean losing the chance to...

options: Let's not assume we must sacrifice one for the other.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Let's press on, Doctor.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Hey, you—

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If you can't stand, stay down.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Reunion... we've met before—

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Oh, you're still here.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: I'll skip asking how you know.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Are you really with Reunion?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Most certainly.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: How many of you are there? Can you help us? There's a weird sickness in the city that isn't Oripathy, and it's spreading!

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: We need to let everyone know, it's not a problem that will affect just a few—

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: There's a few things I need to confirm with you. Can you describe its symptoms?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: It causes green bruises, and your skin slowly rots! My sister caught it, and I sent her to a clinic to 'isolate', but...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: She was taken away, somewhere I don't know. I heard people talking about how they saw soldiers loading Infected onto trucks and sending them to the wall...
Tulin quickly exchanges a glance with Red, as she continues hearing what Tonya has to say without interrupting.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: The soldiers don't let us near the wall, but this time I really wanted to go, no matter what.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I was planning to follow a truck in, so I planted a bomb to distract them, and then I saw—
Tonya's eyes flick to and fro, and finally she looks at Closure.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You saw us?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Yes... I didn't know you, but I guessed we shared a similar goal. It was dangerous, so I just decided on the spot to help you...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Then I missed my chance... the gate's closed.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wow, I really got to hand it to you.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: A plan like that... your bravery is commendable.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We planned it properly and all, you know!

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Um, thank you very much, for saving me...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Could I ask you all... to rescue... my sister...?

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: You said you followed the truck to the wall, but where did it come from?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I don't know, I only realized it was heading towards the wall and followed it.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: So you don't actually know where your sister is.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: I'm sorry, we're willing to offer help to those who need it, but we can't recklessly throw ourselves into danger.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: We can't act without concrete information.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Please, hold on. What happened to this young lady's sister is probably not an isolated case in Zelgrad.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Do you have any idea where your sister might be?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: You're right, I don't have anything solid...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I just thought... she fell sick because I was helping to wash the white coats of those behind the wall. So that's probably the one place they would take her.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: 'White coats', you say?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I think they call them 'researchers', although I've never seen any of them in person. The guards never mention them either.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: They just go 'these are uniforms from Lab Six', 'these are from Test Lab One'...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Hah... it's like we're a laundromat.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: To be honest, we've also observed this 'strange sickness', and concluded that it was already killing the people here, regardless of where it came from.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: And based on what she's said, this is definitely because of an experiment they're running behind the wall...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: —You mean that sickness is really related to the Sarcophagus?

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Uh—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: So you came for the Chernobog Sarcophagus.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hey, don't word it like we're just here for that!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Sorry, I didn't mean it that way.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: We can hear your story later.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: The pressing question now is: what is this 'Sarcophagus' you speak of? What kind of harm could it bring?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's hard to put together a quick and easy explanation, but as far as I know, it's capable of spreading infectious symptoms.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It might not be the same as last time, but something similar did happen before, and just a few years ago too.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Right. All in all, you want to prevent a similar disaster from taking place?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You could put it that way, yeah!

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Is the disaster triggered by this 'Sarcophagus' related to the Infected?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Based on the info we have at the moment, I can't draw any solid conclusions. I can only guess both Infected and non-Infected will be affected.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We're already seeing signs, so we have to look further into it.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Thanks for helping me today, but I'm still going to look for another way to find my friends.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: We tried looking for traces of the refugee miners who came here, but haven't found anything. We haven't looked past the wall, though.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Likewise, we have our duty to fulfill.
Then, count me in too.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Hey, your wounds are serious. Careful how you move.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: I just knew... the First Army's secret weapon work was suspicious, I knew it would kill more civilians than soldiers before it was dropped onto some random battlefield.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: If you plan to cross that wall, then you should let me come with.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: You're an Ursine soldier?

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Heh... have you ever seen an Ursine soldier fall as low as I have?

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: These Reunion people saved me, and I'm grateful.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Bring me along, and I swear you have an ally in me... I won't give up, even if you say no.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: I have a score to settle with a man in there... a man who should have died long ago.

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: Uchitel! There's someone at the right entrance with an identification code requesting entry!

spans.text: There's someone at the right entrance with an identification code requesting entry!

steps.name: Nervous Student
steps.text: It's a complete stranger, so we had her write the code on paper. Here.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: I don't know who this is. Don't let her in.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Seems like this place is no longer safe. We need to move as soon as we can.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Can I see the code?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: This is an old Reunion code.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Someone from your side?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Everyone who followed me to Zelgrad is already here.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Anyone who shows up outside now...

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Talulah.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Yeah, I know. I've heard of her operating in the west.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Let her in.
Her gaze instantly drops to Talulah, but quickly shifts away.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: You—you're the one who warned me!

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: You said you were going to gather more evidence...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: And I'm back with that evidence.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Lyudmila—

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: I don't know what you were talking about, or your plans, but since you've been wandering around the city these past few days—

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: I take it you're looking for those missing Infected.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: You know where they are?

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: I even know of expansion plates in Zelgrad that aren't on any maps.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: On one of those is a factory, where most Infected are sent. As to what the factory is for, I have no clue myself.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: It's tightly guarded, so I came here looking for help, since there's no way I'll manage alone.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: You say those expansion plates aren't on the maps, but wouldn't the residents here notice all their Infected going to the same place?

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: When something doesn't concern them or those around them, it's hard for ordinary people to suss it out.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: After all, Zelgrad is the 'city of tomorrow' where every 'hardworking soul' can find their own place...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: There is no need to worry about those left behind in the cold of winter when you bathe yourself in the warmth of spring.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Regardless, saving as many people as we can is paramount. Before we go past the wall, we need to take a look at that 'factory'.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Having a clear objective simplifies things for us... show us the way.
